name: io.github.Noah-Airmet/pulpit
title: Pulpit
description: Search and quote-check every LDS General Conference talk since 1830, cited to the paragraph.

tools.name: search_concordance
tools.description: Search the exact language of every General Conference discourse 1830–present, paragraph by paragraph. Query language: bare words AND together; "quoted phrases" match exactly; term* is a prefix; -term excludes; uppercase OR for alternatives; a NEAR/8 b for proximity; speaker:name and title:word filter inline. Known archaic spellings (shew/show, labour/labor, Sion/Zion) are searched together automatically and declared. Also searches the talks' endnotes (modern-era citations; editorial notes on early records) — the way to find what a talk cites. Hits say in: "text" (the speaker's words) or in: "note" (with the note number and the paragraph it annotates); in_text/in_notes split the totals. Every hit carries a stable cite URL — use it when quoting.

query.description: concordance query (see tool description for operators)

in.description: all (default), text (spoken words only), or notes (endnotes only)

tools.name: read_paragraphs
tools.description: Read a talk's text by paragraph range, with per-paragraph cite URLs and each paragraph's endnotes. Default 10 paragraphs from the start; page through with from_paragraph/count (max 40 per call).

tools.name: verify_quote
tools.description: Check whether a quotation actually appears in the preached record. Returns an honest verdict: exact, word-forms (stemmed), not-verbatim (closest candidates), or not-found. Checks the spoken text only, never endnotes. Use before repeating any attributed quote.

quote.description: the quotation, without surrounding quote marks

tools.name: talks_by_speaker
tools.description: List a speaker's talks chronologically with cite URLs.

tools.name: list_conferences
tools.description: List conferences in the corpus with talk counts, optionally filtered by era or year range.

tools.name: corpus_stats
tools.description: Edition stamp (which vault commit and date this corpus reflects) and talk counts by era and fidelity.
